NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI accelerator value chain, acting as a fabless semiconductor designer that is critically dependent on TSMC's leading-edge nodes and HBM memory suppliers (SK Hynix, Micron) for its H100/H200/Blackwell GPU production. Its downstream is dominated by hyperscalers (Microsoft, Meta, Google, Amazon) and cloud/enterprise OEMs who are racing to build AI infrastructure, giving NVIDIA extraordinary pricing power but also concentration risk among a handful of mega-cap customers.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly complex global supply chain, acting as a 'fabless-plus' designer that outsources semiconductor fabrication to TSMC and physical assembly primarily to Foxconn, while maintaining tight vertical integration over chip architecture (Apple Silicon) and software. On the downstream side, Apple sells predominantly through carriers, its own retail/online stores, and third-party retailers, while its high-margin Services segment creates a secondary revenue layer from platform participants like Google, Meta, and thousands of App Store developers.

TSM.supply_chain_summary: TSMC sits at the critical nexus of the global semiconductor supply chain as the world's dominant pure-play foundry, translating upstream equipment and materials inputs from a handful of highly specialized suppliers into finished wafers for virtually every major fabless chip designer. Its position is uniquely powerful yet concentrated — extreme customer dependency on Apple and NVIDIA on the demand side is mirrored by an equally critical dependency on ASML's monopoly EUV equipment on the supply side, making geopolitical and single-source risks the defining vulnerabilities of its supply chain.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits in the middle of the semiconductor value chain as a vertically integrated memory manufacturer, heavily dependent on a concentrated set of capital equipment suppliers (ASML, Applied Materials, Lam Research) for its multi-billion dollar fab investments in DRAM and 3D NAND. On the demand side, Micron's revenue is driven by a diverse but concentrated customer base spanning hyperscale cloud providers, AI accelerator vendors, and consumer electronics OEMs, with AI-driven HBM demand from NVIDIA increasingly becoming a high-growth and high-criticality revenue stream.

On the downstream side, IREN monetizes its operations through Bitcoin sales on cryptocurrency exchanges and increasingly through AI/HPC cloud computing services sold to enterprise and hyperscale customers, making its revenue highly sensitive to Bitcoin price volatility and GPU cloud computing demand.

OKLO.supply_chain_summary: Oklo sits at the early-commercialization stage of the advanced fission power value chain, sourcing enriched uranium fuel, specialized nuclear components, and EPC construction services upstream while targeting power-hungry hyperscale data center operators and industrial customers downstream as offtakers for its compact Aurora Powerhouse units. As a pre-revenue company still awaiting NRC licensing approval, its supply chain relationships are largely contractual/LOI-stage, making upstream fuel supply security and downstream anchor customer commitments the most critical near-term risks.
